verdict.rationale: Residency is a fair question for a remote-desktop product, since such products can rely on cloud relays. Sill documents that it has no account and no server, so screen data and keystrokes travel only between the user's own devices. Data residency is therefore whatever hardware and network the user picks, including their own VPN or port forward for remote access, but the product offers no explicit region or storage-location choice. missing for 10: an explicit residency or region control, documentation framing the local-only design as a residency guarantee, independent verification of the no-server claim

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
